item.title: EU commission to propose new tobacco law in ‘early 2027’, reports Rapporteur
item.description: The European Commission is reportedly planning to present its revised Tobacco Products Directive in early 2027, postponing a proposal previously expected before the end of 2026. (Published on November 25, 2026bynewsquawk.com)

item.title: kit ban fails again as pouch proposal advances
item.description: France’s second attempt to ban nicotine vape starter kits has failed on procedural grounds, while a separate proposal seeks to reintroduce nicotine pouches through licensed tobacconists. (Published on November 25, 2026byclearingtheair.eu)

item.title: Portioning out Different Types of E-Cigarettes’ Displacement of Combustible Tobacco in US Adults
item.description: E-cigarettes may be contributing to declining combustible tobacco use in the United States through more than smoking cessation alone. (Published on November 25, 2026byresearchsquare.com)

item.title: ‘The price of switching’: latest GSTHR Briefing Paper brings affordability into focus
item.description: Affordability’s central role in tobacco harm reduction is revealed in the GSTHR’s latest publication,The price of switching: when safer nicotine products cost more than cigarettes. The Briefing Paperquantifies the gap between low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where safer productsusually cost more than cigarettes, and high-income countries (HICs), where safer products oftencost the same or less. Manufacturers’ ambitions to transition away from cigarettes are notcurrently reflected in their pricing strategies for poorer countries. With LMICs home to 4 in 5 peoplewho smoke, affordability is putting harm reduction out of reach in the places that need it most. Download athttps://gsthr.org/ (Published on November 25, 2026bygsthr.org)
